stem: The charge nurse is making assignments in a procedural unit. One RN is newly hired and has not yet completed the facility's competency validation for monitoring clients receiving moderate sedation. Which assignment is most appropriate?

options.A: Assign the RN to monitor moderate sedation independently because an RN license alone establishes competency for every nursing task
options.B: Assign the RN to monitor moderate sedation if the RN agrees to review the policy while the procedure is underway
options.C: Assign the sedation-monitoring responsibility to a nurse whose competency has been verified and give the newly hired RN duties within demonstrated competency
options.D: Assign the RN independently and ask an unlicensed assistive person to observe the client's respiratory status

rationale: Safe assignment requires matching client needs and task complexity with the staff member's allowable duties, demonstrated competency, and ability to exercise appropriate judgment. A professional license does not establish competency for every specialized unit responsibility. When competency for moderate-sedation monitoring has not yet been validated under the facility's process, the charge nurse should assign that responsibility to a qualified nurse and give the newly hired RN work within verified competency. An unlicensed assistive person cannot substitute for the qualified nurse responsible for sedation monitoring.
educational_objective: Charge nurses base assignments on client needs and verified staff competency; specialized monitoring responsibilities should not be assigned independently to personnel whose competency has not been established.
source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing
source_locator: Management of Care — Assignment, Delegation and Supervision, printed p. 20 (PDF page 23): delegate/assign based on client needs and personnel competency; evaluate staff allowable tasks/duties, competency and judgment
source_claim_supported: NCSBN directs the RN to assign/delegate based on client needs and personnel competency and to evaluate allowable duties, competency, and judgment before assignment.

audit_findings.source_audit: Official NCSBN 2026 Assignment, Delegation and Supervision section verified.

audit_findings.choice_A: Incorrect; licensure does not eliminate competency validation for specialized responsibilities.
audit_findings.choice_B: Incorrect; reading a policy during care does not establish validated competency.
audit_findings.choice_D: Incorrect; UAP observation cannot replace qualified sedation monitoring.
audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: Only C ensures the specialized task is performed by verified competent personnel.
